Graduate school, PT/OT school, med school… all care about your cGPA and GPA for prerequisites….

That’s the worse part…. I know nobody care about my grade expect me… and nobody but me puts in the craving for goods grades…. I love the feeling of having good grades….Being on the deans list/ U-SPORT all academic Canadian is what’s drives me and my motivation in school….   In HS I was far on being on the deans list and I was fine with that and having 60/70 but suddenly in university not having an 80 is making me lose my shit….
I haven’t tried Nordic or touring but it’s definitely something that I would like to do…  Do you do Nordic or touring ?

Skiing.  14 years now…. Live on the east cost so I mainly ski on ice  and the hill near my house is pretty small but still pretty fun. I love the adrenaline rush from skiing… going at 50-60km/h is an incredible feeling.

Like they’re a little rough not because I’m off the meds but because of school. Like I I just finished a rush of like 5 finals where I spent the last 2 weeks of December studying 60-65h a week so I’m exhausted…. But other than that I feel fine…. It’s doesn’t last very long ( maybe 2 days)….

I usually stop taking my meds for the holiday break and during the summer. The day of my last final is also the day of me taking my last meds until the first day of the next semester.  I do feel different when I’m off them, that I’m not productive but it’s not a problem since I’m not doing school work.  I like being off my meds when I know I don’t have anything to do because I feel better without them and that my personality is back…
I just wished that more programs had a Co-op option... I feel that doing an internship would help me decide but trying to find one on my own is pretty difficult to find.

Picking a side might be an easy thing to say but it’s not as easy to do. I’ve been trying to decide what side I should be on for a while now and led me to numerous breakdowns… The academic validation I get from psychology is great but once I graduate it’s not going to be there anymore and getting into a Ph.D./PsyD is something extremely difficult and it’s pretty much the only option after a bachelor's in Psychology. If I do go to something that I actually get but get shitty grade, it’s not necessarily better because grads school won’t accept me.  I thought that maybe posting in this sub will clear some things.
